messages:
maria: Heads-up — publishing window tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Registry is enabling org-level quota throttles; we should stagger Py/TS releases to avoid mass 429s and CI storms. Proposed plan: py wheel canary & publish at 09:00, wait 90m, then ts npm publish at 10:30. Keeping canary off by default. @kai @andre

kai: ack. What are the abort/fail-open criteria? How aggressive is the throttle? deploy-bot will surface 429 spikes right?

andre: If deploy-bot reports sustained >5% 429s or >1% error rate for 5m during canary, we abort and pin `stable` back to previous tag. Also plan: 30m holdback between canary -> full for py so we can hotfix wheels (checksum mismatches are common). Can we run a shadow upload today to warm CDN and surface checksum issues?

maria: Good call. I'll run a shadow for wheels at 16:00 today — shadow = upload to staging registry but do NOT promote `latest` tag. Shadow steps (local):

```bash
python -m build
twine upload --repository-url $SHADOW_URL dist/*
```

For npm shadow:
```bash
npm pack && npm publish --registry $SHADOW_REG --tag shadow
```

sara: Quick question: are release notes ready? I pushed a draft at https://internal/release/notes/SDK-1.4.0 — need a deprecation blurb for the sync client and the migration link.

kai: I'll add the deprecation blurb and the migration guide link. Also +1 on the 30-min holdback. For abort strategy: retag `stable` -> `v1.3.8`, block dist-tag `latest` promotion, and require ops approval to republish.

devex-bot: scheduled shadow-upload by maria at 2026-03-21T16:00Z. Will post status in this thread.

deploy-bot: shadow upload succeeded for wheels (sha256:abc123). No CDN propagation errors observed. Shadow npm publish succeeded to shadow registry.

andre: Re: pinning. If we abort, workflow: 1) stop publish jobs, 2) retag stable to v1.3.8, 3) open ticket with `release/abort` label, 4) minor bump and republish as v1.4.1 after fix. Ops approval required to unfreeze dist-tag `latest`. @ops

ops: ack. We'll be on-call for approvals during the window.

maria: Add a preflight check after publish that verifies wheel SHA on PyPI index before promoting. Simple check I want in CI:

```bash
# verify wheel published and sha present on index
curl -sS $PYPI_URL/simple/redwood-sdk/ | grep abc123 || exit 1
```

kai: I'll add that to the publish job and the post-publish monitoring. Also: any objections to holding npm publish back 90 minutes after py publish? This gives time to catch issues without coordinating a rollback across registries.

andre: +1

sara: :thumbsup: I'll add the deprecation note for sync client to the changelog and link the migration guide. Will also draft the customer announcement and drop in #marketing for review after we confirm final tag.

deploy-bot: canary publish for py started at 2026-03-22T09:00Z -> 15% traffic -> no errors observed for 20m. Rolling to 100% after 10m of warm results.

maria: Rolling forward. TS publish scheduled 10:40 UTC (delayed 10m to avoid registry spike). Keep `canary` off for npm; we'll use a staged publish with retries. Watch for 429 patterns in the first 10m.

deploy-bot: npm publish completed at 2026-03-22T10:43Z: 200 packages uploaded, 3 transient 429s automatically retried and succeeded. Final status: OK.

kai: Excellent. No rollback needed. I'll merge release notes and send the customer announcement draft to #marketing.

maria: Thanks everyone — postmortem not required for this window. We'll keep the shadow + preflight checks in the default publish job going forward.

andre: Suggest we codify the 90m gap and shadow step as part of the release runbook to avoid ad-hoc coordination next time.

sara: Agreed — I'll update the release playbook and link it in the notes.
